ai_summary: Great Britain is currently generating 16.2 GW of wind power, with Scotland delivering an estimated 5.5 GW, representing 54.5% of its installed wind capacity. This high volume of renewable generation drives Scotland’s carbon intensity down to 0 gCO2/kWh, compared to 68 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, significant transmission bottlenecks prevent this surplus green energy from reaching southern demand centres. As a result, Scottish generation has seen 27.0 GWh curtailed so far today via the Balancing Mechanism, accumulating a constraint cost of about £1,490,155. If this daily run rate persists, the total yearly curtailment cost would reach approximately £544 million, adding an estimated £2/MWh to consumer electricity invoices across the nation. In addition to the financial cost, this shortfall forces thermal plant dispatch downstream, requiring an estimated 5,134,883 m3 of natural gas to be burned elsewhere to replace the blocked generation. This unnecessary fossil dispatch emits an additional 9,459 tonnes of CO2, highlighting the urgent requirement for accelerated grid reinforcement to alleviate boundary constraints and safeguard both consumer bills and decarbonisation targets.
